note: Seeded rows are a FLOOR, never a cap. Add extension rows with ids X01, X02, ... for any locus the seed missed; extensions have outnumbered seeds in every M3 wave. A cleared claim is a filled cell: write 'no defensible alternative: <reason>' rather than leaving unknown.

rows.locus: resolve grammar: one positional plus required --input plus optional --expected-function-hash
rows.probe: Inspect the `resolve` node from `_parser()`; assert its non-help action destinations and parse `resolve op --input 0` plus each missing-argument case.
rows.reading: D01 fixes one root leaf, one required positional `operation`, one required `--input`, and one optional `--expected-function-hash` whose default is `None`; no fourth argument is admitted.
rows.baseline: Live `_parser().parse_args` at c8b82cd rejects `resolve` as an invalid root command; the leaf and all three destinations are unimplemented.
rows.expected: The action destination set is exactly `{operation, input, expected_function_hash}`; `resolve op --input 0` parses with `expected_function_hash=None`, while a missing operation or input exits 2.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Shipped grammar is exactly that: one positional `operation`, required `--input`, optional `--expected-function-hash` defaulting to None, `allow_abbrev=False`. Deriving the destination set from the node rather than transcribing it is what makes a fourth argument fail the test instead of passing unnoticed.

rows.locus: resolve rejects every option prefix (--in, --exp, --inp) under allow_abbrev=False
rows.probe: Run `main` with full `--input 0` plus each extra prefix `--in 1`, `--inp 1`, and `--exp 00`; inspect status and stderr.
rows.reading: D01 makes `allow_abbrev=False` a property of the new leaf, so every non-exact prefix is rejected even when all required exact arguments are also present.
rows.baseline: At c8b82cd every probe stops earlier because `resolve` itself is an invalid root choice; no resolve option is present to abbreviate.
rows.expected: Each of the 3 probes exits 2, writes no stdout, and includes the exact phrase `unrecognized arguments` plus the supplied prefix on stderr.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, and the probe's construction is why it survives amendment A1. It supplies a full `--input 0` alongside each prefix, which is exactly the condition under which argparse reaches its leftover check. Measured: `--in 1` and `--exp x` both yield `unrecognized arguments: <prefix> <value>` at exit 2 with empty stdout. A prefix-ALONE probe would instead report the missing required option; see A1 and the V18 ruling.

rows.locus: resolve --input - at DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES and at DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES + 1
rows.probe: Patch `sys.stdin.buffer.read`, feed JSON strings of exactly 1048576 and 1048577 bytes through `resolve op --input -`, and spy on `System.resolve`.
rows.reading: D02 reuses `_input` without a second reader: the exact 1 MiB source reaches the library, while the adjacent larger source is rejected before dispatch.
rows.baseline: A live `_input('-')` probe accepts a valid 1048576-byte JSON string and rejects 1048577 bytes as `JSON stdin exceeds 1048576 bytes`; the CLI leaf is absent.
rows.expected: At 1048576 bytes `System.resolve` is called exactly 1 time; at 1048577 bytes status is 2, call count is 0, and the message is `JSON stdin exceeds 1048576 bytes`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `--input` is the shipped `_input` verbatim; resolve adds no reader, so the 1,048,576-byte bound and its message are inherited rather than restated. The adjacent accept/reject pair is the whole obligation - a constant-only pin would pass against a bound the code never applies.

rows.locus: resolve --input malformed JSON: which of _input's three families answers
rows.probe: Run `main(['--db', existing, '--partition', 'tenant', 'resolve', 'op', '--input', '{'])` and capture both streams and the `System.resolve` call count.
rows.reading: D02 routes malformed inline text through the shipped strict parser, so it remains an input-validation failure and never becomes a negative resolve verdict.
rows.baseline: Live `_input('{')` raises `ValidationError` with `invalid JSON: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)`; `resolve` is absent.
rows.expected: Status is 2, stdout is empty, `System.resolve` has 0 calls, and stderr message equals `invalid JSON: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. The invalid-JSON family answers, `System.resolve` is never called, and the message carries the parser's own position text. Pinning the full sentence including `line 1 column 2 (char 1)` is deliberate: it proves the CLI forwards the parser verdict rather than substituting a summary.

rows.locus: a configured candidate source is never called by either new leaf
rows.probe: Inject a source whose `propose` raises, patch CLI `_source` and `System.propose`, then invoke one successful resolve and one successful direct submission.
rows.reading: D03 and D24 forbid candidate-source reach on both channels; direct submission constructs the supplied `Candidate`, and resolve performs only verification plus evaluation.
rows.baseline: Baseline library tests B24 and `test_submit_proposal_never_invokes_a_configured_source` pass with zero source calls; neither CLI route exists at c8b82cd.
rows.expected: Both commands complete with counters exactly `{_source: 0, System.propose: 0, CandidateSource.propose: 0}`; resolve calls `System.resolve` once and submit calls `System.submit_proposal` once.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. This is D24's headline isolation predicate on the resolve side. A configured source must be present for the zero to mean anything, which the probe does, and the counter set covers the builder, the library route and the source object separately.

rows.locus: --db and --partition gate order and exact text on the resolve path
rows.probe: Invoke resolve once with neither global, once with only `--db`, and in both cases supply malformed input while spying on `_input` and `System` construction.
rows.reading: D04 preserves the global gate sequence: database presence precedes partition presence, and both gates precede input parsing, ledger inspection, and construction.
rows.baseline: Live existing-leaf runs return status 2 with `--db or CEMENT_DB is required`, then `--partition or CEMENT_PARTITION is required`; both stdout streams are empty.
rows.expected: The two resolve runs exit 2 with exact messages `--db or CEMENT_DB is required` and `--partition or CEMENT_PARTITION is required`; `_input` and `System` each have 0 calls.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Both gates keep their shipped order and exact text, and both precede `_input` and `System`. Asserting zero `_input` calls is what distinguishes a gate that runs first from a gate that merely runs.

rows.locus: --expected-function-hash mismatch and malformed digest: library-owned verdict and class
rows.probe: Against one promoted set, run resolve with `bad` and with a distinct valid `0` * 64 digest; compare CLI results to direct `System.resolve` results.
rows.reading: D05 forwards the spelling verbatim. A malformed digest is library `ValidationError`, while a well-formed mismatch is a completed failed verification rather than an exception.
rows.baseline: Baseline B15 yields `expected_function_hash must be a SHA-256 hex digest`; B29 yields `passed=False` and `match=None` for a valid wrong digest. The CLI leaf is absent.
rows.expected: `bad` exits 2 with message `expected_function_hash must be a SHA-256 hex digest`; `0` repeated 64 exits 6 on stdout with `passed:false` and `matched:null`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED and it separates the two halves of D05 correctly. A malformed digest is a library ValidationError at exit 2; a well-formed digest that does not match the promoted set is a negative VERDICT at exit 6 with the full payload on stdout. The CLI grades neither - it forwards the value verbatim.

rows.locus: resolve writes no ledger byte, no event, no clock read, no id allocation
rows.probe: Snapshot ledger SHA-256, full `iterdump`, event count, clock calls, and `_new_id` calls before and after CLI hit, miss, and failed-verdict invocations.
rows.reading: D06 makes resolve observationally read-only across every completed state; constructing its response must not use the write-side clock or identifier machinery.
rows.baseline: Baseline B18 proves equal SHA-256 and dump across all 3 library states; the targeted resolve battery also reports zero clock, event, and identifier effects.
rows.expected: For all 3 states, ledger SHA-256 and dump remain equal, event delta is 0, clock-call delta is 0, and `_new_id` call count is 0.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Four independent instruments - ledger digest, ledger dump, event delta and `_new_id` call count - over all three resolve states. The dump matters beyond the digest because a write that restores the previous bytes would defeat a hash alone.

rows.locus: the payload key set is exactly seven keys and identical in all three states
rows.probe: Produce a verified hit, verified miss, and failed verdict; decode each stdout object and compare both its key set and serialized key order.
rows.reading: D07 closes the payload shape over all states. State is represented by nullable values, never by adding or dropping a field.
rows.baseline: The CLI has no resolve payload at c8b82cd; baseline library B05-B07 supplies all 3 distinct `FunctionResolution` states needed by the probe.
rows.expected: Each object has exactly `{artifact_hash, checks, entries, function_hash, matched, output, passed}` and emits those 7 names in that sorted order.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `_emit` sorts keys, so the closed set and the emitted order are one assertion. Requiring the SAME set in all three states is the structural half of D11: a payload that grows a key on a failed verdict would leak the verification shape.

rows.locus: checks projects the ordered [{key, passed, detail}] vector on success too
rows.probe: Run a verified hit, decode `checks`, and compare each projected object plus order to the direct `verification.checks` tuple from the same fixture.
rows.reading: D08 requires the full evidence vector on success and failure. Every check is projected to only `key`, `passed`, and `detail`, preserving library order.
rows.baseline: Baseline B08 returns 6 ordered `FunctionCheck` values on a passing empty set; no root resolve command currently projects them.
rows.expected: `checks` has 6 objects, each with exactly `{key, passed, detail}`; keys begin `duplicate-input-digests` and end `persisted-function-receipt` in library order.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `checks` is `[asdict(check) for check in verification.checks]`, so the vector is the library's own ordering. Pinning first and last key names plus the exact triple field set pins the projection without freezing the six check names as CLI vocabulary.

rows.locus: verified miss is matched false; failed verdict is matched null; the two never collapse
rows.probe: Create one verified miss and one failed verification for the same absent input; compare `passed`, `matched`, status, and the seven-key payloads.
rows.reading: D09 assigns three-valued meaning to `matched`: false proves absence inside a verified set, while null means that verification produced no match object.
rows.baseline: Baseline B06 yields `(passed=True, match.matched=False)`; B07 yields `(passed=False, match=None)`. The library states are distinct before CLI projection.
rows.expected: The miss emits `{passed:true, matched:false}` at exit 6; the failed verdict emits `{passed:false, matched:null}` at exit 6, and neither object equals the other.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. This is the property a shared exit 6 exists to preserve. Both objects carry the same seven keys, so `matched` alone separates a verified absence from a failed verdict, and asserting the two payloads are unequal blocks a regression that collapses them.

rows.locus: output and artifact_hash null-ness tracks match is None exactly
rows.probe: Project a hit, verified miss, and failed verdict; record `(match is None, output is None, artifact_hash is None)` for each state.
rows.reading: D09 requires `output` and `artifact_hash` to project `FunctionMatch` when one exists and to be null when none exists; it does not assert the converse.
rows.baseline: Live B05-B07 observations are hit `(False,False,False)`, miss `(False,True,True)`, and failed `(True,True,True)`, so nullness also occurs with a non-null miss match.
rows.expected: The 3 projected triples are exactly `(false,false,false)`, `(false,true,true)`, and `(true,true,true)`; the locus's claimed iff is false for the verified miss.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, and it forced amendment A4. The row is right that D09's locus sentence overstates: null-ness of `output` and `artifact_hash` tracks `match is None`, while `matched` is null only on a failed verdict. Measured triples of `(matched is None, output is None, artifact_hash is None)` are hit (F,F,F), miss (F,T,T), failed (T,T,T). A4 rules D09's biconditional to bind `matched` ALONE; the other two are null whenever no artifact is projected, which includes the verified miss.

rows.locus: status 0 iff matched is true else 6, with both negative states on stdout
rows.probe: Invoke CLI hit, verified miss, and failed verdict; capture status plus raw stdout and stderr, then decode the output channel.
rows.reading: D10 uses exit 6 as a completed negative verdict for both non-hit states. Resolve never adopts the exceptional stderr channel used by `function export`.
rows.baseline: The CLI leaf is absent; baseline library states report matched values true, false, and no match, while existing function verdict leaves establish stdout exit-6 precedent.
rows.expected: Statuses are exactly `{hit:0, miss:6, failed:6}`; all 3 payloads are JSON on stdout and all 3 stderr streams are empty.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `status=0 if matched is True else 6` is shipped, and the `is True` identity test is load-bearing: `matched` is a tri-state, so a truthiness test would map null to 6 by accident rather than by rule. Both negative states use stdout, never `function export`'s exceptional stderr channel.

rows.locus: no FunctionDocument field reaches stdout on any resolve branch
rows.probe: Use a hit whose verification document contains a planted unique string; scan every state payload recursively and compare its top-level keys to D07.
rows.reading: D11 makes D07's seven-key set closed. The verification document is internal evidence and neither `asdict(resolution)` nor `asdict(verification)` may reach `_emit`.
rows.baseline: Baseline hit and miss `FunctionVerification` values carry a non-null document; failed values carry none. No resolve CLI currently exposes either shape.
rows.expected: All payloads contain exactly 7 top-level keys, contain 0 keys named `document`, and contain 0 occurrences of the planted document-only string.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. The planted document-only string is what raises this above D07's structural pin: a closed key set proves no NEW key appeared, while the planted string proves no document byte reached an EXISTING key.

rows.locus: unregistered operation is 3; empty promoted set and retired-artifact revision are 6
rows.probe: Run resolve against an unknown operation, a registered empty set, and the same operation after `revise_operation` retires its former artifacts.
rows.reading: D12 separates failure to name an operation from two ordinary verified misses. Revision retirement leaves a valid zero-entry current function, not stale state.
rows.baseline: Baseline B28 raises `NotFoundError('operation is not registered in this partition')`; B29 returns a passing zero-entry miss after revision and for an empty set.
rows.expected: Unknown operation exits 3 with `operation is not registered in this partition`; empty and revised cases each exit 6 with `{entries:0, passed:true, matched:false}`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, and the empty-set case is the discriminating one. An empty promoted set verifies successfully and reports a verified absence at exit 6, not an error - `build_function` yields an empty document rather than None, so `matched` is false and never null. A retired-artifact revision reads identically.

rows.locus: an absent --db path answers integrity at 5 and leaves the path absent
rows.probe: Choose an absent path, assert absence, invoke resolve with valid globals and input, then assert status, exact stderr object, and post-call absence.
rows.reading: D13 adds a resolve-only pre-construction existence check and reuses the library's missing-ledger classification instead of allowing `Store` to create a ledger.
rows.baseline: At c8b82cd `System(absent_path)` creates a 208896-byte ledger, while `System.resolve` after deleting an existing ledger raises `ledger file is missing or unreadable`; CLI is absent.
rows.expected: Status is 5, stdout is empty, stderr has exactly `{error, message}` with values 'integrity' and 'ledger file is missing or unreadable', and path existence is false before and after.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Exit 5, the exact two-key stderr object, and path absence BEFORE and AFTER. The after-check is the obligation: D13 exists because `Store` construction would otherwise create the file that resolve was asked to read.

rows.locus: the absent-ledger check precedes --input parsing, so a malformed input creates no ledger
rows.probe: Invoke resolve on an absent path with `--input {`, patch `_input` to raise if called, and inspect status, stderr, `System` construction, and path existence.
rows.reading: D13 deliberately puts the missing-ledger verdict ahead of payload parsing. The precheck prevents both malformed-input work and `Store`'s create-on-construction behavior.
rows.baseline: No resolve leaf exists; direct `System(absent_path)` creates a ledger, and direct `_input('{')` independently raises the stdlib-backed invalid-JSON text.
rows.expected: The command exits 5 with message `ledger file is missing or unreadable`; `_input` and `System` have 0 calls and the absent path remains absent.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Placing the precheck between the `--partition` gate and `System(...)` is what makes D04's ordering safe: with the ledger absent nothing is constructed, so a malformed `--input` rejected later can only ever touch a ledger that already existed. Zero `_input` calls is the ordering evidence.

rows.locus: proposal submit grammar: --sub is unrecognized and `proposal sub` is an invalid choice
rows.probe: Inspect the submit node, parse its full grammar, then run full `--submission {}` plus extra `--sub {}` and separately run `proposal sub`.
rows.reading: D14 adds one exact proposal child with positional `operation` and required `--submission`; neither option prefixes nor subcommand prefixes become aliases.
rows.baseline: Live c8b82cd parsing rejects `proposal submit` and `proposal sub`; the latter says `invalid choice: 'sub' (choose from 'show', 'list', 'review')`.
rows.expected: The action destinations are exactly `{operation, submission}`; full submission plus `--sub` yields `unrecognized arguments`, while `proposal sub` yields `argument proposal_command: invalid choice: 'sub' (choose from 'submit', 'show', 'list', 'review')`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED as revised. The revision is correct and follows A1: `--sub` yields `unrecognized arguments` only when a full `--submission` is also supplied; `--sub` alone reports `the following arguments are required: --submission`. `proposal sub` yields `argument proposal_command: invalid choice: 'sub' (choose from 'submit', 'show', 'list', 'review')`. Both are exit 2 with empty stdout.

rows.locus: --submission - read failure, oversize and invalid UTF-8 answer three distinct messages
rows.probe: Patch `sys.stdin.buffer.read` to raise `OSError`, return 2162723 bytes, and return `b'\xff'`; capture each CLI error after construction and before `System.submit_proposal`.
rows.reading: D15 requires three separate submission-specific families mirroring `_input`, but it does not quote the required prefixes; the ruled spike supplies one concrete wording.
rows.baseline: No `_submission` helper exists. Live `_input` analogues say `JSON stdin could not be read`, `JSON stdin exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and `JSON stdin is not valid UTF-8`.
rows.expected: One concrete reading is exit 2 with respectively `submission stdin could not be read`, `submission stdin exceeds 2162722 bytes`, and `submission stdin is not valid UTF-8`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. The three shipped sentences are exactly `submission stdin could not be read`, `submission stdin exceeds 2162722 bytes` and `submission stdin is not valid UTF-8`. One warning for the battery: the TEXT-stream path says `exceeds 2162722 characters`, so a probe that patches a text `sys.stdin` must expect the characters wording. Mirroring `_input`'s three families with submission-specific nouns is the whole of D15.

rows.locus: the aggregate cap accepts 2162722 bytes and rejects 2162723
rows.probe: Construct valid aggregate JSON at the two adjacent byte lengths, feed each through `--submission -`, and spy on `System.submit_proposal`.
rows.reading: D16 fixes a transport boundary, not a field validator: the exact maximum frame must parse and dispatch, while one additional byte must stop before parsing or library work.
rows.baseline: The submission CLI is unimplemented; tracked envelope probes measured a valid 2162722-byte frame accepted and its 2162723-byte neighbor rejected.
rows.expected: At 2162722 bytes `System.submit_proposal` is called exactly 1 time; at 2162723 bytes status is 2, call count is 0, and the message names `2162722 bytes`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. The adjacent accept/reject pair at 2,162,722 and 2,162,723 is what proves the cap is APPLIED; X11 separately proves it is DERIVED. Neither claim implies the other.

rows.locus: a duplicate envelope key fails inside the parser, before any exact-key check
rows.probe: Submit `{'input':0,'input':1,'output':2}` with JSON quotes, patch any post-parse key checker to raise, and capture the first verdict.
rows.reading: D17 requires `parse_json` to receive the raw aggregate before object construction; its duplicate-pairs hook therefore owns the error and no last-wins object exists.
rows.baseline: Live `parse_json` raises `duplicate JSON object key: 'input'`; proposal submit is absent, while ordinary argparse repeated flags remain last-wins.
rows.expected: Status is 2 with exact message `duplicate JSON object key: 'input'`; post-parse key-check and `System.submit_proposal` call counts are both 0.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `parse_json` is strict, so `{"input":1,"input":2}` fails inside the parser with `duplicate JSON object key: 'input'` before the exact-key check runs. That ordering is D17's reason for existing: a permissive parser would silently keep one of two values and the key check would see a well-formed envelope.

rows.locus: unknown keys and missing keys each name every offending key, sorted
rows.probe: Submit one object with unknown keys `z,a` and all required keys, then one object missing `output,input`; capture complete messages and dispatch counts.
rows.reading: D18 fixes exhaustive sorted key names but not the surrounding sentence. The ruled envelope spike offers one wording, while other prefixes satisfy the binding text.
rows.baseline: No envelope validator exists at c8b82cd. The tracked envelope alternative uses `submission has unknown keys: a, z` and `submission is missing keys: input, output`.
rows.expected: The shipped wording exits 2 with `submission has unknown keys: a, z` and `submission is missing required keys: input, output`; `System.submit_proposal` call count is 0 for both.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED as revised. The shipped sentences are `submission has unknown keys: a, z` and `submission is missing required keys: input, output` - the word `required` is present, and the pre-revision expectation would have gone red against correct code. Both lists are sorted and exhaustive, and `System.submit_proposal` is never called.

rows.locus: a non-mapping provenance answers the library's own message at exit 2
rows.probe: Submit an envelope whose provenance value is `[]`; spy on `System.submit_proposal` while allowing its real candidate validation to run.
rows.reading: D19 deliberately leaves provenance shape to `_canonical_candidate`; the CLI constructs `Candidate` without pre-coercing or replacing a non-mapping value.
rows.baseline: Live direct `System.submit_proposal` rejects list provenance with exact `candidate provenance must be a mapping`; no CLI route exists.
rows.expected: The command exits 2 with exact message `candidate provenance must be a mapping`, writes no stdout, and leaves request, proposal, and event deltas all 0.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Provenance shape stays library-graded: `candidate provenance must be a mapping` comes from `Candidate`, not the CLI, and the CLI adds no coercion. Zero request, proposal and event deltas prove the rejection precedes the write.

rows.locus: success emits exactly one key, proposal_id, and never the bare returned string
rows.probe: Patch `System.submit_proposal` to return `prop_probe`; invoke a valid submission and compare decoded stdout plus its raw JSON shape.
rows.reading: D20 wraps the library's bare identifier in one stable binding key and rejects both direct `_emit(id)` and any constant status decoration.
rows.baseline: Live `_emit('prop_probe')` writes the bare JSON string `"prop_probe"`; direct `System.submit_proposal` returns a `prop_` string. The CLI route is absent.
rows.expected: Status is 0, stderr is empty, and decoded stdout equals exactly `{proposal_id: 'prop_probe'}` with 1 key and no `status` key.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Exactly one key. The bare string `submit_proposal` returns is not emitted directly because `_emit` would render it as a keyless JSON string, and the flags patch's `"status": "review_required"` stays REJECTED: every successful submission is pending by construction, so that key would advertise a variability the API does not have.

rows.locus: an unregistered operation on submit is 3 and writes zero rows
rows.probe: Snapshot every application-table count, submit a valid envelope for an unknown operation, then compare status, exact error, and all table deltas.
rows.reading: D22 preserves the library's `NotFoundError` class after envelope validation. The write transaction rolls back before any request, proposal, or event survives.
rows.baseline: Direct `System.submit_proposal` raises `operation is not registered in this partition` and the M3.3 battery records zero durable rows; CLI submit is absent.
rows.expected: Status is 3 with message `operation is not registered in this partition`; all 13 application-table deltas, including requests, proposals, and events, are 0.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Exit 3 with zero rows across all 13 application tables. Sweeping every table rather than the expected three is what turns this from a spot check into a footprint claim.

rows.locus: two byte-identical submissions return two ids and write two of each row
rows.probe: Invoke the identical submit command twice against one registered operation; compare proposal identifiers and the application-table delta from the pre-call snapshot.
rows.reading: D23 explicitly rejects idempotency. CLI wrapping must not deduplicate, synthesize a request key, or turn the second successful write into a replay.
rows.baseline: Live direct library test `test_identical_content_submitted_twice_writes_two_of_everything` passes with distinct proposal and request identities.
rows.expected: The 2 stdout `proposal_id` values differ; cumulative deltas are exactly `{requests:2, proposals:2, events:2}` and 0 for every other application table.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. This is D23 stated as an observable rather than a warning: two byte-identical submissions, two distinct ids, exactly two of each of the three rows and zero elsewhere. There is no idempotency and the battery says so in deltas.

rows.locus: the parser census moves 28 to 30 leaves and 35 to 37 nodes, derived from _parser()
rows.probe: Recursively walk every `_SubParsersAction` from `_parser()`, deriving leaf paths and total parser nodes without a transcribed expected path list.
rows.reading: D25 adds exactly two leaves and their two parser nodes: root `resolve` and nested `proposal submit`; no existing leaf is removed or split.
rows.baseline: Live recursive census at c8b82cd reports 28 leaves and 35 nodes, with 28 distinct existing paths.
rows.expected: The derived census reports exactly 30 leaves and 37 nodes, and set subtraction against the 28-path baseline yields exactly `{'resolve', 'proposal submit'}`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, re-derived by MAIN from `_parser()` at e6ba873: 30 leaves, 37 nodes, and the set difference against the 28-path baseline is exactly {'resolve', 'proposal submit'}. The census MOVING is the obligation landing, not a regression; deriving it inside the test rather than transcribing it is why the number can be trusted.

rows.locus: cross-leaf option isolation holds in both directions for both new options
rows.probe: Supply `--submission` to resolve and `--expected-function-hash` to proposal submit while all legitimate required arguments are present; scan every other leaf too.
rows.reading: D26 makes option ownership exact: the expected hash belongs only to its shipped function leaves plus resolve, while submission belongs only to proposal submit.
rows.baseline: Neither new option owner exists. Existing parser inspection shows `--expected-function-hash` only on three function leaves and no `--submission` action anywhere.
rows.expected: Both cross-new-leaf probes exit 2 with `unrecognized arguments`; across all 30 leaves `--submission` occurs 1 time and the expected-hash option occurs 4 times.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Isolation in both directions is the point: `--submission` must not appear on any other leaf and `--expected-function-hash` must stay off `proposal submit`. The count of 4 for the expected-hash option covers its pre-existing homes plus resolve, so the battery derives it from the census rather than asserting a bare 1.

rows.locus: CLI eager JSON parsing cannot preserve the library-owned expected-hash-before-input precedence
rows.probe: On an existing valid ledger, invoke resolve with `--expected-function-hash bad` and malformed `--input {`; record which exact error reaches stderr first.
rows.reading: D05 says expected-hash validation precedes input and is library-owned, while D02 requires `_input` to turn CLI text into a value before `System.resolve` can be called. Ordinary Python argument evaluation therefore reverses the edge unless the CLI duplicates a library validator or the API changes.
rows.baseline: Direct baseline B16 reports `expected_function_hash must be a SHA-256 hex digest` before rejecting an invalid input object; no CLI route exists to parse raw JSON.
rows.expected: Literal D05 requires exit 2 with `expected_function_hash must be a SHA-256 hex digest`; the straightforward `_input(args.input)` dispatch instead yields the invalid-JSON message first.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, and it forced amendment A2. Measured: `--input '{bad' --expected-function-hash bad` exits 2 with `invalid JSON: ...`, while `--input 1 --expected-function-hash bad` exits 2 with `expected_function_hash must be a SHA-256 hex digest`. A2 narrows D05 to the truth: the library owns precedence AMONG library validations, and CLI value-parsing necessarily precedes all of them because a value must exist before `System.resolve` can be called. Duplicating `_digest` in the CLI to restore the literal edge is REJECTED - it would put a second copy of a library validator on the surface D05 exists to keep thin.

rows.expected: The minimum-count map is `{union_cells:2, per_file_cells:8}`: union needs each spelling somewhere, while per-file needs both spellings in all 4 files.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED as a real ambiguity, resolved by amendment A6 in favour of the UNION. Measured cells for (`cement resolve`, `cement proposal submit`): README (1,1), architecture (1,1), threat-model (1,2), adapter-protocol (0,0). A6 rules the union over README, docs/architecture.md and docs/threat-model.md, with README additionally required to carry both; docs/adapter-protocol.md is OUTSIDE the union because it documents the adapter protocol and names no CLI leaf. The per-file reading is rejected on merits: it would force redundant grammar transcription into documents whose job is not teaching invocation, and duplicated grammar is exactly what goes stale.

rows.locus: every placeholder in each shipped shell block is produced earlier inside that same block
rows.probe: Parse every shipped shell block, identify uppercase or REPLACE_ME-style consumers, and trace each to an earlier command output or assignment within its block.
rows.reading: D29 prohibits copy-paste examples that require hidden state from prose or a prior block. A listing or inspection command may produce a later identifier if the relation is explicit.
rows.baseline: Existing README blocks include `prop_REPLACE_ME`, `HASH_FROM_INSPECT`, and `HASH_FROM_VERIFY`; their earlier producer relationships must survive or be made explicit when blocks change.
rows.expected: The derived orphan-placeholder set is exactly `{}` across all shipped command blocks, including every new resolve and proposal-submit example.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. The single placeholder in the new blocks is `HASH_FROM_VERIFY`, and its producer `function verify support.reply` is the FIRST line of the same block, with the prose above naming it. Two derivation warnings MAIN measured the hard way: a naive fence regex spans fence boundaries and reports prose words such as `LLM`, `OCR` and `README` as placeholders, and placeholders inside inline code in prose - `request REQUEST_ID`, `events --after SEQUENCE` - are outside D29's scope. The battery must walk fences line by line and consider shipped command blocks only.

rows.locus: published resolve cost figures are mechanically derived from the committed benchmark artifact
rows.probe: Load `m3u2b-resolve-bench.json`, derive the stated precision for each entry count, and compare every resolve-cost prose figure to those values.
rows.reading: D30 binds operator claims to the end-to-end `resolve_cold_hit_ms` measurements, not to copied literals or component estimates. A mismatch must fail loudly.
rows.baseline: The committed points are 5.736265 ms at 1, 613.17169 ms at 1000, and 36452.212317 ms plus 985696 KiB peak RSS at 50000.
rows.expected: Prose derives exactly `5.7 ms`, `613 ms`, `36,452 ms` or `~36.5 s`, and `985,696 KiB` or `~963 MiB` from those 3 artifact points.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. All four figures derive from `m3u2b-resolve-bench.json` at the precision each entry count states: 5.7 ms at one entry, 613 ms at 1,000, 36,452 ms and 985,696 KiB at 50,000, matching the method docstring's ~36.5 s and ~963 MiB. Deriving rather than transcribing is D30's mechanism - a re-measurement then moves prose and artifact together or fails loudly.

rows.locus: resolve help and operator prose never characterize the full verification as fast cheap or cached
rows.probe: Collect the resolve help text and every prose sentence naming the command; case-fold and search the prohibited cost adjectives while requiring the full-verification warning.
rows.reading: D30 prevents read-only from being misread as inexpensive. Resolve performs all six checks on every call and caches nothing.
rows.baseline: No resolve CLI help or command prose exists; the library docstring already says one call runs full verification, costs ~36.5 s at 50000, writes nothing, and caches nothing.
rows.expected: Counts of `fast`, `cheap`, and affirmative `cached` claims are all 0; at least 1 help or prose surface states `six` checks or `full verification` and `caches nothing`.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED with the shipped sentence named. `fast` and `cheap` are absent; the two `cached` occurrences both describe WITHHOLDING cached output on the reconciliation path and are not affirmative claims about resolve. The positive half is shipped as `Cement caches no verification between calls.` in README alongside `One resolve runs the full six-check verification, so it costs what function verify costs.` The battery must match those meaning-bearing tokens, NOT the literal string `caches nothing`, which appears only in the method docstring. This row is D27's rule applied to cost: `resolve writes nothing` invites a cheapness inference that only the caching sentence closes.
